summary.oneLiner: One of India's leading industrial gases and engineering companies, part of the global Linde network, serving metals, manufacturing, healthcare, chemicals, refining, electronics, food processing and infrastructure customers.
summary.business: Linde India operates through two segments: Gases & Related Products, which supplies oxygen, nitrogen, argon and specialty gases via onsite pipeline systems, bulk liquid distribution networks and packaged gas solutions (including a healthcare portfolio of medical gases for hospitals), and Project Engineering, which designs and delivers air separation plants and engineering solutions supporting industrial development. As part of the global Linde plc network, the company combines international capabilities with local market insight.

currentContext.strengths: Part of the global Linde plc network, combining international capabilities with local market insight|Extensive production and distribution network across national ASU/PGP sites and manufacturing works|24x7 Customer Service Centre and the Linde Connect digital platform enabling order management, delivery tracking and inventory monitoring, strengthening customer stickiness|Deep engineering expertise supporting design and delivery of air separation plants (Project Engineering division)|In-house innovation capability (e.g., Linde Mixer ACMG 50/100 gas-blending equipment developed by the C&MES team)|Strong balance sheet, diversified portfolio (Gases + Project Engineering) and deep customer relationships (per Chairman's message)
currentContext.strategies: Strengthen leadership in the Gases business across Onsite, Merchant Bulk and Packaged segments|Expand presence in key industrial clusters, particularly the Dahej cluster in Gujarat|Invest in supply chain resilience and operational efficiency, including downstream logistics infrastructure|Leverage opportunities in high-growth and emerging sectors such as semiconductors, electric mobility, renewable energy and advanced materials|Advance sustainability and energy transition initiatives, including expanding renewable energy sourcing and hybrid renewable energy arrangements under long-term contracts|Expand the specialty gases portfolio and focus on high-value, differentiated offerings (particularly Argon) in Packaged Gases|Deepen customer engagement in the healthcare segment through medical conferences, training programs and technology demonstrations|Deepen customer relationships and enhance customer experience via structured CX measurement (annual CX surveys)|Company follows a policy of consistent dividend payment, striving to declare a steady stream of dividends keeping shareholders' long-term interest in mind, balanced against the amount of profit retained in the business, per its Dividend Distribution Policy (effective from 11 February 2017). The Company reasonably expects to continue declaring dividends in future unless restrained by loss/inadequacy of profits or unforeseen circumstances.
currentContext.expansion: During FY2025-26 the Company commissioned a new debulking facility at Lucknow (catering to LOX, LMO, LIN and LAR) and a Lucknow-Kanpur debulking station (commercial operation from September 2025), commissioned a high-purity nitrous oxide (N2O) purification unit at Hyderabad (August 2025) serving Solar and Electronics customers, and capitalised the IOCL Panipat nitrogen (N2) project in October 2025. Capacity expansion initiatives remain on track with a new 250 tpd Air Separation Unit (ASU) at Dahej scheduled for commissioning in FY2026-27, building on the faster-than-anticipated ramp-up of the previous Dahej ASU. Separately, to support a long-term pipeline gas-supply project with Asian Paints (Polymers) Private Limited, the Company is setting up its third ASU at Dahej (245 TPD liquid plus 100 TPD gaseous oxygen), currently under implementation. The Company has also approved an ammonia purification project in Gujarat expected to be commissioned in FY2026-27, undertook capacity enhancements at Baroda with a planned expansion roadmap for new Packaged Gas Plant (PGP) sites, and continued investing in special-gases distribution assets (silane tube trailers, an ammonia ISO tanker and an N2O tube trailer) aggregating approximately Rs. 374 million.
currentContext.mdna: India's GDP growth remained around 7%, supported by robust domestic consumption|Manufacturing sector's share of GDP stays broadly range-bound at 15%-17%, though local value addition in manufacturing is growing|Traditional core industrial sectors (steel, refinery, automotive, construction) showed steady growth, while sunrise sectors such as solar and semiconductor saw high double-digit growth|'Make in India' mission, PLI schemes, ease-of-doing-business reforms and infrastructure/logistics cost reduction expected to drive a wide range of investment and manufacturing activity|Onsite Gases demand tied to commercialization of new capacities supporting expansion plans of large Steel and Refinery customers|Merchant Bulk achieved highest-ever liquid loading volumes in FY26, reflecting strong demand across key industrial sectors|Liquid Nitrogen demand outpaced Liquid Oxygen for the second consecutive year, driven by electronics and food & beverage sectors|Electronics segment demand benefited from photovoltaic (PV) solar capacity expansion and new semiconductor packaging investments|Liquid Argon demand supported by metal fabrication, stainless steel, electronics, solar sectors, and low-carbon ferro-alloy manufacturers|Packaged Gases growth driven by high-value/differentiated offerings, particularly the Argon product portfolio|Healthcare segment continued to perform strongly on active customer engagement initiatives|External environment carries uncertainties (geopolitical developments, commodity price volatility) but the structural growth story of the Indian economy remains intact|Project Engineering division supported by a healthy order pipeline linked to long-term industrial investments|Secured new greenfield projects in the solar segment under long-term contracts of five years|Secured the largest Medical Gas Pipeline System (MGPS) order in India, from DRFMS Hospital, Mumbai

risks.note: Increasing trade protectionism, geopolitical tensions and uncertainties in international markets pose risks to supply chains, energy markets and capital flows; a slowdown in global economic growth could affect demand from key industrial sectors, and currency fluctuations may impact input costs.

risks.risk: Domestic inflation and energy cost risk
risks.note: Inflationary pressures in key commodities and rising energy costs are a concern given the energy-intensive nature of industrial gas production.

Performance is closely linked to core sectors such as steel, refining, chemicals, healthcare and infrastructure; a slowdown in these sectors could reduce demand. The business model, including long-term onsite supply arrangements, exposes the Company to customer concentration and sectoral cyclicality.
Capacity additions by industry participants may exert pressure on pricing and margins.

risks.risk: Operational risk at production and supply chain facilities
risks.note: Supply chain disruptions, availability of critical equipment, and reliability of large production facilities such as Air Separation Units may affect plant uptime and service delivery.
Increasing digitalization of operations exposes the Company to cyber-attacks on plants and business systems, which could impact business continuity if not adequately managed.

Exposure to environmental and climate-related risks, including those arising from the transition towards a low-carbon economy and increasing regulatory focus on sustainability; regulatory or policy changes may also influence infrastructure spending, an important demand driver.

The Company was in receipt of an Order (ref. WTM/AB/CFID/CFID-SEC3/30578/2024-25 dated 24 July 2024) passed by SEBI under Sections 11(1), 11(4) and 11B of the SEBI Act, 1992; the Directors' Report states there were no significant/material orders impacting going-concern status, but the order itself is disclosed.

themes.title: Industrial gases, chlor-alkali & commodity chemicals
themes.need: A capacity-led commodity-chemical and industrial-gas cycle underpins the basic-materials chain - ELLEN on air-separation/industrial gases; EPIGRAL/CHEMPLASTS/DCW/DCMSHRIRAM/GHCL/TATACHEM/GNFC on chlor-alkali, soda-ash and vinyls; LORDSCHLO on caustic; CHEMBONDCH on water-treatment chemicals. Pricing/utilization and energy costs are the near-term swing factors.
themes.driver: Caustic/soda-ash price recovery; utilization ramp on new capacity; energy-cost relief.
